tabs.title: Understanding the text
tabs.description: Read for meaning and significant details.

tabs.title: Real-life decisions
tabs.description: Apply a useful idea in a new setting.

questions.q: What is the main change the organisers make for the new festival?
choices: They cancel the concerts.
They offer reusable cups instead of relying on disposable ones.
They stop visitors from bringing drinks.
They move the festival to a different town.
questions.explanation: The festival tries a reusable cup deposit system to reduce rubbish.

questions.q: Why do volunteers add clearer signs and another return desk?
choices: The festival is expecting no visitors.
The water stations have been closed.
The organisers have run out of cups.
Some guests are worried they will have to wait in long lines.
questions.explanation: The additional signs and return desk are a response to concerns about queues.

questions.q: Why do some children become interested in collecting used cups?
choices: They must help the cleaning team after school.
The cups have different colours they can exchange.
They can receive the deposits as pocket money.
They need to take the cups to the water station.
questions.explanation: The children can keep the two-euro deposits when they return abandoned cups.

questions.q: What shows that the cup system is a partial success rather than a perfect solution?
choices: Fewer cups are left, but some disappear and other rubbish remains.
The team cannot find any returned cups at all.
The cleaners have to work later than last year.
Every food seller has already changed their packaging.
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph reports improvements while acknowledging missing cups and food wrappers.

questions.q: Why is borrowing a cup different from buying a disposable one?
choices: The reusable cup belongs to the visitor forever.
The visitor can return it and receive the deposit back.
A reusable cup can never be damaged.
The festival pays every visitor two euros to drink.
questions.explanation: Returning a borrowed cup makes its deposit refundable and encourages reuse.

questions.q: Why does the smaller number of rubbish bags matter?
choices: It proves that visitors bought fewer tickets.
It shows the concert had fewer food stalls.
It provides evidence that the festival produced less collected waste.
It means every visitor returned a cup.
questions.explanation: Counting rubbish bags offers a measurable comparison with the previous year.

questions.q: Why do organisers plan to speak to food sellers next year?
choices: They want to close every food stall.
They need to increase the price of music tickets.
They believe food should not be sold at concerts.
They have noticed that wrappers and plates remain a significant problem.
questions.explanation: After cup waste falls, packaging from food is still present in the collected rubbish.

questions.q: A school event removes disposable cups but leaves food wrappers everywhere. What lesson fits the article?
choices: One successful change does not solve every type of rubbish.
Visitors should not be allowed to drink water.
The organisers should stop counting rubbish.
Reusable cups make waste collection unnecessary.
questions.explanation: The festival's organisers recognise that cup reuse helps but does not eliminate other waste.

questions.q: People avoid water stations because they cannot find them. What solution follows the festival's example?
choices: Ask every visitor to buy a separate bottle.
Place clear signs where people need them.
Remove the stations and save money.
Keep the stations hidden to avoid long lines.
questions.explanation: Volunteers use signs to make facilities easy to find.

questions.q: Which next improvement is most consistent with the organisers' plan?
choices: Tell cleaners not to collect wrappers anymore.
Remove all return desks from the event.
Change the music programme rather than waste management.
Work with food vendors to reduce packaging and add bins near food.
questions.explanation: The organisers specifically plan less food packaging and more bins near the food area.
